primitives.name: Objective Purpose Fact
primitives.verbatim_quote: In a word, the fact of purpose, as we conceive it, is an objective fact.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P ∈ {0,1} represents presence of purpose; E ∈ ℝ^n denotes objectively determinable end vector.
primitives.assumptions: Behavior is responsive to externally defined goals; purpose is not subjective or mentalistic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When behavior becomes non-responsive to external ends, indicating loss of objective purpose.

layer2.mapping: The objective purpose fact is isomorphic to a probabilistic constraint on behavioral response functions in GSI's Bayesian framework.
layer2.telemetry: Observable behavioral consistency relative to goal vectors.

primitives.name: Behavioral Docility
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is the fact that behavior is docile relative to objectively determinable ends.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: B(t) ∈ ℝ^m denotes behavior state at time t; E ∈ ℝ^n denotes end vector; D(B,E) ∈ [0,1] measures docility.
primitives.assumptions: Behavior adapts to externally imposed objectives; adaptation is measurable and quantifiable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss of docility when B(t) ceases to respond predictably to E.

layer2.mapping: Behavioral docility underpins GSE's kernel of state transition dynamics, where E drives B(t+1).
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between behavioral change and end vector variation over time.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P ∈ {0,1} indicates purposive behavior; B(t) ∈ ℝ^m denotes behavior; E ∈ ℝ^n denotes end.
primitives.assumptions: Psychological phenomena are reducible to behavior; purpose is embedded in behavior, not in mind.

The failure mode occurs when the system assumes mentalistic causation instead of objective behavioral responses, breaking the isomorphism between behavior and purpose. This triad avoids metaphysical bifurcation by grounding all concepts in observable behavior and deterministic relationships.
